newsitem.title: EGYPT: Sudanese leader predicts uprising at home.
newsitem.headline: Sudanese leader predicts uprising at home.

text.p: Sudanese opposition leader Sadeq al-Mahdi predicted on Saturday that there would be an uprising in Sudan by students, workers, civil servants and professionals.
In a speech in Cairo to exiled members of his Umma Party, Mahdi said that most members of these groups were with the opposition and ready for change.

"The active sectors such as students, who are playing a vanguard role, and the street and the workers, and also the civil servants and professionals will play a vanguard role in the coming uprising," he said.
"There is no doubt that all these sectors are now very ready for change, and by a big majority," he added. His remarks appeared in an Umma Party statement on the meeting.

Mahdi, who was prime minister of Sudan when President Omar Hassan al-Bashir took power in a military coup in 1989, arrived in Cairo on Friday from Eritrea. He fled across land to Eritrea earlier this month after years under surveillance in Khartoum.
While in Sudan, Mahdi refrained from advocating violence to overthrow Bashir's government. On arrival in Asmara he said he wanted to change the government with a minimum of bloodshed.
